entries.title: Promises made in a crisis
entries.odia: ଆତଙ୍କ ବେଳେ ଯାଚନ୍ତି କୁକୁଡ଼ା, ଆତଙ୍କ ଗଲେ ଦିଅନ୍ତି ନେଫେଡ଼ା
entries.literal_meaning: In a crisis they promise a chicken; when the crisis passes they give “ନେଫେଡ଼ା” (the final noun is left untranslated because its meaning is unresolved here).
entries.explanation: The source explains this as a vow made to God during danger and neglected once the danger passes. More broadly, it can remind someone not to forget a promise after receiving help. The precise meaning of the final noun is unresolved; the interpretation follows the supplied gloss.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିପଦ ବେଳେ କରିଥିବା ମାନସିକକୁ ବିପଦ ଟଳିଗଲେ ଭୁଲିଯିବା କଥା ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଅଛି। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ପାଇବା ପରେ ଦେଇଥିବା କଥା ଭୁଲି ନ ଯିବା ପାଇଁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଶେଷ ଶବ୍ଦଟିର ସଠିକ୍ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: After asking for urgent help and promising to return it, someone stops answering once their own problem is solved. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The religious vow is the source’s explanatory setting, not a recommendation or a claim that everyone follows this practice. A previously deferred dictionary saying has different wording; no equivalence or repaired final word is certified.

entries.title: Only you know what is in your heart
entries.odia: ମାଲୁଣି ହାତରେ ଲଙ୍କା ମରିଚଲୋ, ମାଳି ହାତେ ଫୁଲ ହାର, ଯାହା ମନ କଥା, ସିଏ ଜାଣେ ସିନା, ତାହା କି ଜାଣିବ ପର ॥
entries.literal_meaning: Chillies in the woman gardener’s hand, a flower garland in the gardener’s hand: each person knows their own thoughts; how would another know them?
entries.explanation: The closing lines remind us that another person’s private thoughts are not directly visible. The everyday objects lead into that contrast; this reading does not assign a hidden moral meaning to the chillies or garland. Ask rather than assume what someone feels.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣେ ମଣିଷର ମନ କଥା ସେ ନିଜେ ଜାଣେ; ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ତାହା ଆପେ ଜାଣିପାରେ ନାହିଁ। ତେଣୁ କାହାର ଭାବନା ବିଷୟରେ ଧରିନେବା ଅପେକ୍ଷା ତାଙ୍କୁ ପଚାରି ବୁଝିବା ଭଲ। ଲଙ୍କା ଓ ଫୁଲହାରକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଅଲଗା ନୈତିକ ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A friend seems quiet after receiving good news. Rather than decide that they are ungrateful, you ask what is on their mind. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Listed as a saying in this community anthology; author, earliest use and possible song or literary relationships remain unverified. Gardener words are translated as occupational imagery, not evidence about any community’s traits.
